--- name: pstack description: "Pick a pstack method before a non-trivial task: a bug or failing test, code you have not read, a multi-file or batch change, writing or changing tests, an API or shared-state change, a measured number, a review, a hard multi-part job, or calling work done." allowed-tools: Bash(bash *pstack-path.sh) --- pstack folder `

`: !`bash ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/pstack-path.sh` If the folder line above is empty or not an absolute path (you read this file directly, not through the Skill tool), run: jq -r '.plugins["pstack@cursor-plugins"][0].installPath' ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json - Skip this skill when your brief came from a pstack skill or already names the method. - Read each chosen `

/skills//SKILL.md` in full and follow it. Read `

/docs/harness/claude-code.md` only when that skill says to. - Never call the Skill tool on a `pstack:` skill. Never use setup-pstack, poteto-help, sharpen, in-your-own-words or make-bot-ui. - A skill marked (spawns) starts agents. In the main session, state the agent count first, then hand the task and the skill path to one `worker`. A worker runs it within about a dozen agents. Without the Agent tool, use the skill's one-context prompt in its `references/`, or do the delegated role yourself in one context: interrogate's adversary work too, never skipped. - poteto-mode only for a contested design, concurrency or a cross-cutting change (standing ruling: 1.9x cost, no quality gain in the pilot). Stop before any push or PR that a playbook asks for. - When two rows fit, take the higher row, and also read every principle whose line fits. | Situation (broad to narrow) | Skill | |---|---| | A hard multi-part job or large migration | figure-it-out (spawns) | | A contested design, concurrency or a cross-cutting change | poteto-mode (spawns) | | Several competing designs | principle-exhaust-the-design-space; arena (spawns) | | Explaining a change or subsystem to the owner | teach | | Many similar units | principle-build-the-lever; swarm (spawns) | | A bug or failing test | principle-fix-root-causes; tdd for a cheap local test; principle-attack-the-premise after two failed fixes | | How or why code works | how, why (spawns) | | A multi-step change | principle-sequence-verifiable-units | | A measured number | principle-explain-the-number; benchmark-checklist for a timing | | Shared, retried or concurrent code | blast-radius; principle-make-operations-idempotent; principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state | | Merged code changed what a formal-verification skill models | maintain-formal-verification-skill | | A diff you do not trust | interrogate (spawns) | | A long or unattended run | show-me-your-work (spawns 1) | | Before saying done | principle-prove-it-works | Principles: - principle-attack-the-premise: two fixes on one premise failed - principle-boundary-discipline: wiring validation, error handling or adapters - principle-build-the-lever: work a script could do or prove - principle-encode-lessons-in-structure: the same correction a second time - principle-exhaust-the-design-space: novel architecture or UI, no precedent - principle-experience-first: product, UX or feature-scope tradeoffs - principle-explain-the-number: measuring, trusting or reporting a number - principle-fix-root-causes: debugging any symptom - principle-foundational-thinking: choosing core types and data structures - principle-guard-the-context-window: large outputs or long files fill context - principle-laziness-protocol: refactoring, or tempted to add a layer - principle-make-operations-idempotent: steps that must survive crashes, retries - principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis: new internal API, old callers remain - principle-minimize-reader-load: code that is hard to trace - principle-model-the-domain: stateful logic or heavily branching code - principle-never-block-on-the-human: tempted to ask about reversible work - principle-outcome-oriented-execution: planned rewrites and migrations in phases - principle-prove-it-works: before declaring done - principle-redesign-from-first-principles: a new requirement in an existing design - principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state: concurrent writers to one file or key - principle-sequence-verifiable-units: multi-step work, stacked commits or PRs - principle-subtract-before-you-add: sequencing an addition, refactor or rewrite - principle-test-behavior-not-implementation: writing, changing or keeping a test - principle-type-system-discipline: designing types or function signatures
